feature: Core evaluator for core-pilot and core-shrink (eval)
label: executable
evidence: Goose/Core/Eval.lean; pilot goldens first, range_loop and sampled_extent; 40+ #guard programs in Goose/Core/Examples.lean; shrink execution guards in Goose/Core/ShrinkChecks.lean; both numeric profiles
limits: Fuel is evaluation depth plus loop iterations. Call nesting over maxCallDepth (100000) is a timeout at every fuel, so a deeply recursive terminating program has no done result. Storage is unbounded: no out-of-memory, no stack exhaustion. Store.write checks neither type nor mutability: an unchecked module can store a value of another type and run to done.
assumptions: None: a definition.
witnesses: Goldens and #guard programs in Goose/Core/{Examples,ShrinkChecks}.lean. The semantic corpus harness result remains pilot-only; shrink qualification uses focused guards and separate source/Core/GIR/native fixtures.

feature: Core validator for core-pilot and core-shrink (validate)
label: executable
evidence: Goose/Core/{Typing,Roots,Validate,ShrinkChecks}.lean; test/semantics/malformed/INDEX; proved sound for accepted Core modules by TH-SAFE-01
limits: Changed while proving soundness, each in the rejecting direction: a global initializer now gets the root and effect pass and may reach only earlier globals (two accepted modules faulted: rejected_call_global_init_derefs_later, rejected_call_global_init_param_annotation); a call charges the caller with the globals the callee context lists for a parameter its summary names; a by-value loop over a run and an append count as a read of the run (rejected_summary_omits_loop_read); a summary may not name a parameter index past the parameter list (the decoder already refuses it); the root pass rechecks declaration order, which the typing pass already guarantees. The pilot harness result is unchanged (54 agree, 0 mismatch, 4 unsupported). V-MUT is not used by any proof. ValidateAgrees (Guarantees.lean) is a statement only. References to slice variables: a by-reference parameter may have type ref (slice T); its context annotation carries content roots (optional third field of vr); reads through it yield them, stores through it must lie within them, and a call requires them to denote exactly the root set of the slice variable passed, each root outliving it. No expression yields such a reference as a value, so it exists only as a parameter. The pilot harness is unchanged until the exporter emits the form; Share/Writer.lean does not write content roots, and lower emits GIR-H that gir-validate rejects (GIR-V010). After review: the contents of a let array are writable (a run sampled from a variable or global is mutable whatever its kind; assigning the variable as a whole still needs var); a writable reference or slice may initialize, rebind or be returned as a read-only one; a call of a context found never to return (its body always exits, aborts or makes such a call, with only plain statements before) ends a path; loop variables are numbered before the variables their bounds or run declare, as the tag table says. Still rejected though the compiler accepts: test/typing/return_const_recursion.goose, whose export declares a writable reference result and returns a read-only one; with the result declared read-only it validates and runs to the compiler's output. V-MUT has no semantic theorem: the evaluator has no read-only storage.
assumptions: None: a definition.
witnesses: Accepted and rejected modules in Goose/Core/{Examples,ShrinkChecks}.lean and every rejected_* line of test/semantics/malformed/INDEX. The semantic corpus harness result remains pilot-only.

label: model-proved
statement: If Store.append o vs succeeds, every location that was readable is still readable, and every readable location that is neither the grown array nor an ancestor of it reads the same value. Typed form: if o has type grow E and the new elements have type E, every typed location stays typed, o stays grow E, the new elements are read at o++[n+i], and the store refines the old one.
differs_from_target: The target 'read (push s o v) l = read s l' is false for the grown array and its ancestors, whose content is the array, so those are excluded; the statement is about Store.append (the operation eval uses), not a separate push. Val.resizable now records its element type so that growing an empty array cannot change which array type it has.
assumptions: Typed form assumes the elements have the element type.
witnesses: sampled_extent golden: reference to element 0 read after a push; forms1 growing loop
evidence: Goose/Proofs/Memory.lean, audited.
limits: True in the model by representation: a location is a root and an element path, not an address. That the production data stacks keep elements in place is not covered.

label: model-proved
statement: For m with validate m = .ok (), a numeric profile p, there exist plans with deriveModuleDemand m = .ok plans and PlansWellFormed m plans such that, for every fuel n, Specs m p plans n. Specs gives a Sat theorem for each of the fourteen Core evaluation functions under its checked occurrence, effect, permission, demand, observation, and frame premises: faults are excluded; successful results restore the specified frame and store invariant, observed values/roots, retained aliases, and effect footprint. In core-shrink, StoreInvAt requires live-location validity only for demanded locals (globals remain live); retained references/runs are tracked separately. Shrink checks exclude demanded or retained interior aliases that may overlap a grow-shrink shrink, while whole-owner references remain valid; limited aliases retain written physical slots across visible-length reductions. Parameter roots remain conservative where context evidence does not prove distinctness.
differs_from_target: The formal claim is the per-fuel Specs family, not an unconditional state-transition theorem. Its StoreInv live-reference clause is demand-aware, so dead reference values may remain stored after a shrink; validity is not required for every stored reference or every visible variable. Sat permits abort, exit, and timeout, and its postcondition applies only when the evaluator returns normally; it excludes faults but proves no post-state invariant for a stopped computation.
assumptions: Only module acceptance is needed to obtain validated_steps_keep_invariant. Each Specs clause has explicit premises for the syntax/type and root replay at that occurrence, effect inclusion, the frame and observation state, and (for core-shrink) classified parameters and shrink protection.
witnesses: Goose/Core/ShrinkChecks.lean: positive last-use, loaded-scalar, limited-kept-reference, whole-owner, and by-value-iteration runs; V-SHRINK rejections for live, loop-carried, retained-argument, retained-run, and call aliases; V-SUMMARY omission rejection. Goose/Core/Examples.lean includes a forged-root module that faults when run without validation.

reviewer.lane: independent review_core, source review after upstream rebase
reviewer.verdict: sound and meaningful for accepted Lean Core pilot and shrink modules

answers.1: Accepted last-use, loaded-scalar, limited retained-slot, whole-owner and shrinking-call witnesses satisfy validation and run in both numeric profiles. Negative guards reject demanded aliases and omitted summaries.
answers.2: Sat excludes faults and states normal-return postconditions. ModOk derives from checker acceptance; derived well-formed demand plans precede the all-fuel Specs proof. No circular safety premise occurs.
answers.3: checkContext computes body effects with rpBlockValue and checks supplied summaries with checkSummary. Unknown summaries and possibly overlapping parameter roots remain conservative.
answers.4: No-fault safety allows aborts, exits and timeouts. The invariant concerns demanded locations and retained aliases, not universally unchanged contents. Neither theorem establishes termination, output, mutability or construction cost.
answers.5: Only transparent Lean Core validate and eval are covered. GIR lowering, production C++, native execution and G-SHRINK remain outside scope.
answers.6: Source inspection found no new axioms, sorry, unsafe, opaque or native decision shortcuts. Exact-source builds and transitive axiom checks use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

label: model-proved
statement: For every Lean Core Module m, validate m = .ok () implies Goose.Core.WellFormed m. WellFormed conjoins declarative table validity, implementation and global typing, context and global root judgments, and demand protection. Tables include unconditional origin-record validity, local and global origin bounds, dense scopes, resolved types, descriptor layout, implementation coverage, and entry shape. Context roots include a body traversal and containment of its computed effects in each known summary.
differs_from_target: The target implication is proved for the modeled core-pilot and core-shrink syntax. The declarative judgments reuse Core syntax, environments, type operations, effect substitution, and demand extraction. They are separately defined propositions, not a separately implemented language specification. Demand additionally retains PlansWellFormed as an explicit conjunct.
assumptions: Only validate m = .ok (). There is no caller-store, evaluation, termination, or trusted-summary premise. The proof derives each WellFormed field from acceptance.
witnesses: Goose/Core/WellFormedChecks.lean accepts an empty pilot module and a shrinking clear with its shrink summary. It proves that a mistyped store, forged roots, and an omitted shrink summary cannot satisfy WellFormed. Goose/Core/DeclarativeTablesChecks.lean rejects unused bad origins and malformed layouts. Goose/Core/DeclarativeDemandChecks.lean checks retained aliases, conservative parameter overlap, and failed source extraction. Existing Core/Examples.lean and Core/ShrinkChecks.lean supply larger accepted programs. Goose/Core/OriginsChecks.lean proves malformed origin records cannot satisfy WellFormed and checks decoder/validator rejection.

reviewer.verdict: sound and meaningful for the Lean Core model; no P1 or P2 defect found

answers.1: Yes. Acceptance is the only premise. Existing guards accept pilot programs and a shrink clear with the required summary. WellFormedChecks also proves independent negative judgments for all three target counterexamples.
answers.2: WellFormed exposes six concrete fields. Typing is a proposition-valued traversal whose equivalence to the checker is proved, rather than assumed. Roots separately state root containment, outliving, escaping-result restrictions, and body effects. Tables state bounds and layout propositions, including every origin record even when unused. Demand shares expected-point extraction and includes PlansWellFormed, but also requires source totality, coverage, and explicit alias separation. No field assumes WellFormed or semantic safety.
answers.3: Each context supplies a RootBlockValue derivation for its implementation body. SummaryContains requires the resulting effects to lie within each known summary, including shrinks, aborts, outputs, and rebinding. Calls substitute callee annotations and summaries. Every context is checked, so recursive summaries require mutual closure rather than trusted partial results. Unknown summaries remain conservative and are not asserted precise.
answers.4: This is static acceptance soundness. It proves no final value, identity preservation, termination, construction cost, or execution result. Summary abort and output flags conservatively contain body effects. Semantic no-fault and caller-state preservation claims remain separate Safety theorems.
answers.5: The theorem concerns transparent Lean Core validate and WellFormed definitions. It proves neither production C++ checker correctness nor exporter, decoder, GIR lowering, native layout, or profile-wide conformance. It covers no core-construction syntax.
answers.6: The proposition-valued Judgment and RootRelation monad instances were inspected. Their pure, bind, and state operations encode equality and existential composition. WellFormed and its judgments are transparent definitions with no local notation, opaque replacement, or native decision shortcut. The registered theorem's transitive axioms are checked by Goose/Audit.lean against propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

reviewer.checks: Passed sequential lake --rehash --verbose olean builds for the transitive Audit closure, DeclarativeTablesChecks, DeclarativeDemandChecks, and WellFormedChecks. OriginsChecks also passed its focused olean build. Actual compiler invocations use lean -j1 -M4096. validate_wellFormed and the three target negative judgments report only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Audit elaboration accepts the new registry entry. git diff --check passed. The executable audit and production compiler tests were not run by this lane.

label: model-proved
evidence: For modules m, m' with equal implementation tables, globals and entry, and contexts that name the same implementation at every index, eval n p m = eval n p m' for every fuel n and numeric profile p. The erased fields are every Context field other than impl: decl, varRoots, resultRoots. eval_eraseRoots instantiates it with a module whose contexts have no declaration key and no roots.
limits: The target says replacing a module's context table changes no result; proved: replacing it while keeping each context's implementation index and the entry. A different implementation index is a different program (TH-SHARE-01 covers the case where it is justified). files, types and origins are not constrained because eval reads none of them; origins are read only by the tool when it prints a line number.
assumptions: None beyond the Core definitions of eval.
witnesses: Goose/Share/Examples.lean: the first golden with its root annotations erased is rejected by validate and runs to the same output.

label: model-proved
evidence: If Quotient m m' q rho holds then eval n p m = eval n p m' for every n and p. Quotient: header tables, entry and globals of m' equal those of m; m' has the contexts of m at the same indices with impl mapped by q; every implementation f a context of m names is, in m, the body m' holds at q f with its callees renamed by rho f; rho f sends each context to one that m' maps to the same implementation. The proof is a simulation by induction on fuel over the evaluator's mutual definitions, so mutually recursive groups need no separate argument.
limits: Differs from the target in three ways. (1) Bodies name contexts, not implementations, so the renaming that makes two bodies equal acts on context indices (rename by rho f, chosen per implementation: identity or a representative map) instead of one map q on implementation indices; q maps only the implementation index of each context. (2) Nothing is demanded of implementations no context names, which a run cannot reach; quotient_of_implwise gives the plan's every-implementation form when every context names an existing one. (3) Globals, files, types and origins must be equal (no merging of global initializers).
assumptions: None beyond the Core definitions of eval.
witnesses: test/semantics/share/INDEX (checked by run_index.sh) and Goose/Share/Examples.lean: issue-9 shape, free variable bound to two locals, mutually recursive pair, merge after one round; counterexamples: bodies differing in one operation and callees that differ stay distinct, forged merges are rejected, and the forged modules behave differently.

feature: a quotient of a never-faulting module never faults
label: model-proved
evidence: If Quotient m m' q rho and eval n p m is never a fault, then eval n p m' is never a fault. share_validated_never_faults takes the safety statement (validate m = ok implies no fault at any fuel and profile) as an explicit hypothesis and concludes the same for a validated m.
limits: The safety theorem remains an explicit hypothesis. TH-SAFE-01 now supplies that hypothesis for the same Core eval. The quotient m' is not claimed to validate: renaming callee contexts in a merged body can name a context whose annotations do not suit every caller context.
assumptions: TH-SAFE-01 (hypothesis of share_validated_never_faults).
witnesses: Goose/Share/Examples.lean: the proposals of the fixtures validate and run to the unshared output.

label: model-proved
evidence: checkQuotient m m' qt rt = true implies Quotient m m' (fun f => qt.getD f f) (bodyRenaming m m' _ rt). The witnesses qt and rt are untrusted: a wrong one makes the check fail.

Completeness (every quotient has witnesses the checker accepts) is not proved; goose-semantics share rebuilds the witnesses from the context tables and accepts the proposer's output and the fixtures. Bodies are compared with the implementation name, variable names and summary, so functions that differ only in a name are not merged.
assumptions: None.
witnesses: test/semantics/share/INDEX: three forged claims rejected, proposals accepted.

label: executable
evidence: goose-semantics share --propose merges implementations by structural equality of bodies, refining from one group to the coarsest self-consistent grouping, so a call cycle merges as a whole; a group whose members already agree keeps its body untouched. The result is always passed through the checker.
limits: Untrusted. Quadratic in call-chain depth (one round per level): 400 levels took 4 s, 3000 flat contexts 0.3 s. Not proved coarsest.

label: model-proved
theorem: Goose.Reuse.cachedRun_result, cachedRun_consistent, cachedRuns_agree, cachedRuns_agree_from, cachedRun₂_result, cachedRuns₂_agree
evidence: If the key determines the result and the cache is consistent, cachedRun returns the uncached result and leaves the cache consistent; any sequence of cached runs from the empty cache (or any consistent cache) returns the uncached results; two stages in a row, the second keyed on the first's result, have the same property.
limits: A cache is an association list (entries are only added for absent keys). The model is independent of Core and says nothing about any real stage.
assumptions: KeyDetermines: key i = key j implies run i = run j, which is the completeness of dependency tracking. Assumed, not proved; see the next row.

feature: key completeness of a reuse boundary
label: assumed
evidence: The hypothesis cannot be dropped: if the key does not determine the result there is a consistent cache and an input for which cachedRun answers wrongly; concretely, inputs (0,0) and (0,1) with key = first component.
limits: Establishing KeyDetermines for a real boundary is per-boundary work (native objects by construction; whole build through the recording reader; checked results not established).

feature: GIR-H interpreter, validator and Core lowering
label: executable
evidence: Goose/GIR/{Syntax,Eval,Validate,Json,Effects}.lean, Goose/Lower/CoreToGir.lean; test/gir/golden/check.sh (27 modules agree with Core in both numeric profiles, lower is deterministic and round-trips); test/gir/invalid/check.sh (38 modules); a one-off run of about 3000 generated Core programs agreed in both profiles (generator not committed)

label: model-proved
statement: moduleOk m = true -> eval n p m = done o t -> exists k, GIR.run k p (lower m) = done o t, for every Core module m, numeric profile p, fuel n, outcome o and output t.
differs_from_target: Only the decidable moduleOk fragment. Initializers and entry expressions include scalar operations, references, fields, slices, aggregate literals, conditionals and block expressions. Entry statements include assignments, append, pop_n, resize, clear, whole replacement, conditionals, while, print, assert, abort, exit and return without a value. Local declarations, rebinding, calls, range, foreach, explicit return values, break and continue are excluded. The entry has no parameters. Core faults are not shown to lower to faults.
assumptions: moduleOk m = true (decidable, checked on goldens in Goose/Lower/Witness.lean). The interpreter takes the type of an integer operation from its operand, as Core does, so no typing hypothesis is needed in the fragment. The proof is by induction on Core's fuel over simulation claims for every syntactic category; the IR's fuel is existential (the claims give an equation that holds for every additional unit of fuel, so no separate fuel-monotonicity result is used). The blocks a fragment creates are handled by a builder relation (LS.Adv in Goose/Lower/Frag.lean: a fragment grows the block table, leaves every existing block but the current one unchanged, and ends in no block, its own block or a block it created) proved for every fragment of the lowering; the finished function's table extends the table at every point of the lowering (ExtT). The IR's next instruction no longer faults at a type's maximum (it adds one): the loop theorem cannot hold at every fuel otherwise, because Core's model allows an array longer than a counter type's range, and a for-range loop whose bound is such a length reaches the maximum. No fragment of this stage uses next; the change is recorded here because it alters the interpreter and the specification text for i_next ('a counter at the maximum is a fault'), which this lane does not own.
witnesses: Goose/Lower/Witness.lean checks legacyControlModule: a let-free conditional, false while and unit return are inside moduleOk, accepted by both validators, and return matching output in both profiles. Earlier declaration-bearing goldens are explicitly outside legacyCovered while retaining Core acceptance and execution agreement guards. Runtime agreements do not establish fragment membership.
reviewer: Independent lower review found the unrestricted declaration/rebinding claims false after readonly destination coercion; those claims were narrowed and their consumers migrated. The integrated 205 changed Lean roots and their 296-module closure passed at a45f1f76. Whole-profile typed lowering remains incomplete.

Typed whole-profile composition still needs generated-state authority and final inferred-type facts. label: model-proved
statement: validate m = ok implies, for every function: each block has exactly one terminator and it is last; every defining instruction is typed by Op.resultTy from the types of its operands and the recorded type is that type; every instruction that can abort or stands for a statement carries an origin; each implementation's summary contains the effects the provenance analysis finds. For constants, integer arithmetic, comparison, boolean negation and conversion, running on a frame whose operand cells hold the derived types finishes or aborts at an origin and never faults.
differs_from_target: Dominance and scope balance are not proved to follow from acceptance: both checks run iterative analyses (dominator sets, the scopes entered at each block) and their soundness is not argued. Typing is semantic only for the scalar operations above; memory, call and view operations are not. Reference lifetime is not implied: test/gir/invalid/gir_accepted_dangling_reference.json is accepted and its run faults with dangling_root. Summary closure is relative to the validator's own analysis.
assumptions: None beyond validate m = ok; the scalar theorem assumes the operand cells have the derived types.
witnesses: 38 modules in test/gir/invalid, each failing at the check its name gives, one accepted and faulting

label: model-proved
statement: For every fuel n and enclosing loop context lc, a Core while statement with exprOk condition and blockOk body is simulated by its actual lowerStmt output in any extending finished function, under the Rel frame/environment relation. Normal completion produces normal unit and Post; abort and exit preserve their final state and trace.
differs_from_target: A local statement simulation, not the module theorem. Its body and condition use the established fragment, which excludes nested loops and calls; break, continue and return are excluded. moduleOk still excludes while statements.
assumptions: exprOk condition, blockOk body, actual builder equation, a live initial builder point, ExtT of the finished function, and Rel between Core environment and GIR frame. No validation or termination assumption.
evidence: Goose/Lower/While.lean; added to the axiom audit; proof by induction on Core fuel. Goose/Lower/Witness.lean checks a three-iteration counting while from gir_loop_small, confirms its condition/body satisfy the local theorem predicates, and confirms Core/GIR agree with output 3 in both numeric profiles.
limits: Says nothing about faults, timeouts, divergence or the concrete compiler exporter/emitter. Does not claim whole-profile lowering.

reviewer.verdict: sound-and-meaningful within the recorded fragment and conditional premises

answers.1: Yes. The counting-while golden, reduced to three iterations, has exprOk condition and blockOk body and agrees at done/returned/output 3 in both numeric profiles. A separate concrete false-condition while instantiates stmt_while_sim with actual lowerStmt output, ExtT from finishBlocks, a live initial point and Rel. PreRel is satisfiable by placing each initial value in its indicated frame cell and declaring its variable in the entered block scope. The conditional loop lemmas permit useful header/body invariants but do not establish them for concrete range lowering.
answers.2: No whole-loop conclusion is hidden. Claims and BlockPreClaim expand to actual builder equations, ExtT, Rel and SimG. SimG requires continuation equations for every initial store and final-state equality for abort/exit; Post preserves the initial frame prefix and scope relation. WhileCondition/WhileBody and RangeBranch/RangeBody explicitly assume simulations of strictly smaller condition/body steps and a back edge; fuel induction composes them. These are conditional composition lemmas, not discharged range lowering. Same is only equality of frame value cells below a frontier, not a memory-store or reference-lifetime guarantee.
answers.3: No validator or effect-summary acceptance is assumed or concluded by these seven claims. Rel matches numeric profile, slots, activation, scopes, depth and builder scope stack; it does not assume a semantic effect summary.
